free_tier.stated: No free tier. The cheapest 1-year token is USD 52: the order page lists 'yearly - $52 (4 devices)' as a PayPal subscription and 'one year - $52 (4 devices)' as a single order; the same page lists 'two years - $94 (5 devices)', 'monthly - $6 (1 device)' and 'weekly - $1.86 (1 device)'.
free_tier.notes: Prices are read from the order forms of the vendor's home page. The FAQ states a device limit that depends on the token's duration: one year gives 4 WireGuard keys and 4 OpenVPN sessions.

retention.stated: not applicable: a tunnel, not stored bytes
retention.notes: The FAQ states the servers keep no logs that identify a customer; no stored-object retention applies.

egress.terms: No byte cap and no throttling are stated: the FAQ answers 'Are there any speed/traffic limits?' with "No. We don't do any kind of throttling/QoS." Servers are 1 Gbps, and 10 Gbps at five named sites; bandwidth is shared with other servers in the same cabinet.

interface_detail: A tunnel, not a data API: OpenVPN (ECC and RSA configurations) and WireGuard, authenticated with a token. Protocols: OpenVPN and WireGuard. UDP: the home page states 'UDP or TCP (1-65535)', so both transports run on any port. Port forwarding: yes, from 30000 to 65535, enabled at http://10.31.33.7/fwd inside the tunnel, 100 forwards per internal IP on each server. SOCKS5 endpoint: unverified: no page read states one. Obfuscation: SSH, HTTPS (Xray or stunnel) and obfs4. BitTorrent: allowed ('BitTorrent allowed').
tooling: Any OpenVPN or WireGuard client with the vendor's published server configs; the vendor states all server-side configs are public. Port forwards are made from a web page reachable only inside the tunnel. The vocabulary has no wireguard, openvpn or socks5 interface token, so the interface list says unknown.
chaining: A tunnel exit for traffic that must leave from a shared VPN address: a job connects with a token, and the upstream sees one of the provider's shared addresses (over 450 IPs listed).

limits.value: none published: "No. We don't do any kind of throttling/QoS."; servers are 1 Gbps (10 Gbps at Switzerland, Finland, Atlanta, Chicago and Oregon)
shared exit addresses: 'Currently over 450 available IPs', used by many clients at once, so destination-side limits and reputation on an address apply to every client behind it

limits_note: Concurrent connections are capped by token length and the vocabulary has no kind for it: a one-week or one-month token allows 1 WireGuard key and 1 OpenVPN session, a one-year token allows 4 and 4, a two-year token 5 and 5, a lifetime token 6 and 6.
binding_note: No byte quota, speed cap or request rate is published; the only stated ceiling is the concurrent-session count of the token, which the limit vocabulary cannot name.

identity_cost.detail: A token is the account. The order page's Monero form is labelled 'no 3rd parties, no email or JS required', and the vendor states it accepts Monero 'so people can order an access token anonymously without providing any personal information'. Card and PayPal orders go through PayPal or CCBill, and only recurring subscriptions get the token by email; other orders show it in the browser. The vendor states it has no KYC policy.

reliability_note: The FAQ states servers share bandwidth with other servers in the same cabinet, so peak hours can lower speed; port forwards are per server and have to be recreated when moving to another server.
confidence_note: Documented: price, protocols, UDP, port forwarding, obfuscation and the BitTorrent line are quoted from the vendor's own home page, FAQ and port-forwarding page. Nothing was connected through the service, so no speed, address class or forwarding behaviour is measured. A SOCKS5 endpoint is unverified because no page read mentions one.
price_per_tb_month: USD 52 for a 1-year token (4 devices); a subscription price, not a per-TB price
